# Use brand-kit

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Capture a brand once as a reusable brand.json — logo files (and an on-dark version), colour roles as hex codes, heading and body fonts, voice, imagery rules, a PowerPoint template, contact details and the legal footer — plus a one-page BRAND.md, with text contrast checked and every value traced to where it came from.

**Reach for it when** the user wants decks, flyers or documents in their branding, says "use our brand", "here's our logo and colours", "set up our brand kit", or hands over brand guidelines.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install brand-kit                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install brand-kit --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install brand-kit --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Design pack: [`--pack design`](../packs/use-the-design-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/design/skills/brand-kit/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Here's our logo and brand colours — set up a brand kit we can reuse"
- "Use our brand guidelines PDF so everything matches our style"
- "Capture our fonts, colours and logo rules in one place"
- "Make our decks and flyers on-brand — start with the brand settings"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Build a PowerPoint deck for the board meeting"
- "Make a flyer for our open day"
- "Design a new logo for my startup"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use brand-kit".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every colour is a hex code with a role.** "Our green" is not a brand colour; `#0E5A46` used for title bars is.
- **Text on background passes 4.5:1,** checked by the script rather than by eye.
- **Every value says where it came from,** and inferred values are marked as inferred.
- **Logo files are real paths that exist,** with a PNG for PowerPoint and an on-dark version when the brand has one.
- **Nothing is invented.** A field the user didn't supply and couldn't be read from their sources is left out and listed, not guessed.
- **BRAND.md fits on one page.** A person checks the brand from it without opening the JSON.

## Use something else when

- Designing a new brand from scratch: this captures a brand, it doesn't invent one
- Building the deck itself; convert its Markdown with `md-to-pptx`
- A one-off document where the user only wants the default look
